I reviewed the actual diff (not the self-report), read the standing SUPERBOSS_DISPATCH_PROMPT.md rules, cross-checked the credit-accountant.py call against its only other real call site (preflight-guard.py), traced the clarification-gate logic against `query.py`/the mandatory-gate doc, and ran the new test suite locally (5/5 pass).

**Verdict: reject** (tier1 — this only means "not ready to auto-merge," the PR stays open with review comments per the reject policy).

Key findings written to `review-verdict.json`:
1. The new `--mode owner-dispatch` path never checks `needs_owner_clarification` before auto-dispatching a real task — bypassing the mandatory clarification gate the runbook itself documents as a precondition.
2. The `start` auto-dispatch branch fires immediately after `submit` without checking `submit`'s own `duplicate_found` signal, undercutting the standing NO DUPLICATION/NO COLLISION rule.
3. Repo auto-selection silently defaults to `claude-control` with no real override checkpoint, despite a comment claiming one exists.
4. The bundled credit-accountant.py fix passes an untested `--repo` flag not used by the only other existing caller — it may silently no-op, leaving the claimed gap unfixed.

The core wiring code itself (routing/dispatch logic, shared section-list dedup, TASK_ID entity extraction) is clean and well-tested — the issues are specifically about safety gates being skipped now that this path is being promoted to the "preferred" real entrypoint for live Owner messages. No `.github/workflows/**` changes present.
